findings.evidenceJa: ここで倒される訳にはいかない
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he cannot allow himself to be defeated here.
findings.explanation: The English narrows defeat to death and overstates the immediate outcome.

findings.highlight: I can get there in one step if I jump with all my strength
findings.evidenceJa: 全力で跳び退けば一足で脱出できる
findings.governingReading: With a full-force backward leap, Shirou can escape the shed in one bound.
findings.explanation: The English loses the direction and turns a single bound into the ambiguous “one step.”

findings.highlight: Rider can close the distance long before I get outside
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の跳び退くスピードより、ライダーの詰め寄ってくるスピードの方が速い
findings.governingReading: Rider’s closing speed is faster than Shirou’s backward-leap speed.
findings.explanation: The English changes a comparative speed disadvantage into a much larger “long before” timing gap.

findings.highlight: hostility that can be taken as anger or dejection
findings.evidenceJa: 怒りとも落胆とも取れない殺気
findings.governingReading: Rider leaks killing intent whose affect cannot be read cleanly as anger or disappointment.
findings.explanation: The English again softens imminent lethal intent into hostility.

findings.highlight: she looks like a giant snake
findings.evidenceJa: 闇に佇み、獲物を狙う姿は巨大な蛇のよう
findings.governingReading: Standing in darkness and aiming at her prey, Rider resembles a giant snake.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the simile but removes the still hunting posture and Shirou’s status as prey.

findings.highlight: concentrate only on the signs of her attack
findings.evidenceJa: 鎌首をもたげる予兆だけに意識を集中し
findings.governingReading: Shirou focuses on the first sign of the figurative snake raising its head to strike.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the carried snake image and exact anticipatory motion with generic attack signs.

findings.highlight: I jump out into the yard
findings.evidenceJa: かすかに興奮しながら
findings.governingReading: Shirou retreats into the yard with faint excitement at succeeding.
findings.explanation: The English removes the first affective beat before the narration explains his rising pulse.

findings.evidenceJa: ライダーの短剣を躱せた
findings.governingReading: Shirou is excited that he evaded Rider’s dagger despite her superior ability.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the concrete weapon and actor with a generic attack.

findings.evidenceJa: 隙をついて土蔵から脱出できた喜び
findings.governingReading: His joy comes from exploiting an opening to escape the shed.
findings.explanation: The English removes the tactical opening that made escape possible.

findings.governingReading: Shirou tells himself that is as far as he can celebrate or rejoice.
findings.explanation: The English uses “pleasure,” giving the combat reaction an inappropriate sensual or indulgent shade.

findings.highlight: I don’t feel anyone coming after me out of the shed
findings.evidenceJa: 追って来る気配がない
findings.governingReading: Shirou senses no sign that Rider is pursuing him.
findings.explanation: The English describes nobody emerging toward him from the shed, weakening the specific chase relation.

findings.evidenceJa: 現れた時のように、夜の闇へ消えて行った
findings.governingReading: Rider vanishes into the night in the same manner as she appeared.
findings.explanation: The English removes the deliberate symmetry between her entrance and departure.

findings.evidenceJa: ライダーの気配が遠ざかっていく
findings.governingReading: Rider’s presence grows more distant as she leaves.
findings.explanation: The English makes the sensed departure instantaneous and loses its direction and progression.

findings.evidenceJa: それが俺の思い違いでなければ
findings.governingReading: Shirou cautiously allows that his belief Rider spared him may be his own mistake.
findings.explanation: The English recasts a self-doubting interpretation as a suspicion that may be correct.

findings.evidenceJa: 彼女も力を貸してくれるかもしれない
findings.governingReading: Shirou thinks Rider may lend him her strength if a trigger arises.
findings.explanation: The English expands the beneficiary from Shirou to his group.
